notes:
Potential & Potential Energy

  • Potential due to a point charge: $V = \dfrac{kq}{r}$; potential is a scalar, $V=0$ at infinity.
  • $\vec{E} = -\dfrac{dV}{dr}$ (field points from high to low potential); work done in moving a charge $q$ between two points $= q(V_A-V_B)$, independent of path.
  • Potential energy of two charges: $U = \dfrac{kq_1q_2}{r}$. For a system of point charges, sum over all pairs.
  • Potential due to a dipole: axial $V = \dfrac{kp}{r^2}$ (for $r\gg a$), equatorial $V = 0$.

Equipotential Surfaces

  • Always perpendicular to field lines; no work done moving a charge along one; surfaces are spheres for a point charge, planes for a uniform field.

Conductors

  • Electric field inside a conductor (electrostatic) is zero; the entire conductor (surface + interior) is at the same potential; charge resides only on the outer surface; field is strongest where curvature is highest (action at points).

Capacitance

  • $C = Q/V$, SI unit farad (F). Parallel plate capacitor: $C_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$ (vacuum); with dielectric $K$ filling the gap: $C = \dfrac{K\varepsilon_0 A}{d} = KC_0$.
  • With a dielectric slab of thickness $t < d$ partially filling the gap: $C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - t + t/K}$.

Combinations

SeriesParallel
Formula$\dfrac1C=\dfrac1{C_1}+\dfrac1{C_2}+\dots$$C=C_1+C_2+\dots$
Same on allcharge $Q$voltage $V$

Energy

  • Energy stored: $U = \dfrac12CV^2 = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C} = \dfrac12QV$; energy density $u = \dfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2$.
  • Charging a battery-connected capacitor with dielectric: $V$ constant, $C$ and $Q$ increase by factor $K$, energy increases by $K$.
  • Isolated (charge constant) capacitor with dielectric inserted: $Q$ constant, $C$ increases by $K$, $V$ and energy decrease by factor $K$.
  • Van de Graaff generator: builds up very high potential (few MV) by continuously spraying charge onto a large hollow conducting sphere, used to accelerate charged particles.

Exam tip

KCET typically asks 2–3 questions from this chapter, usually a potential-due-to-charges numerical, a series/parallel capacitor combination, and one on dielectric effect or energy stored. Watch for the battery-connected vs isolated-capacitor distinction — a classic trap.

questions.q: The electric potential at a point 20 cm from a point charge of 4 $\mu$C is
questions.explanation: $V = kq/r = 9\times10^9\times4\times10^{-6}/0.2 = 1.8\times10^5$ V.
questions.trick: $V=kq/r$ — potential is scalar, just divide, no direction needed.

questions.q: Two point charges of $+2\,\mu$C and $-2\,\mu$C are placed symmetrically 10 cm apart. The potential at the midpoint of the line joining them is
questions.explanation: Potential is scalar: $V = kq_1/r + kq_2/r$; equal and opposite charges equidistant give $V = 0$ (unlike the field, which is non-zero there).
questions.trick: Equal-opposite charges equidistant: potentials cancel (scalar) even though field doesn't.

questions.q: A charge of 5 $\mu$C is moved from a point at potential 200 V to a point at potential 50 V. The work done by the electric force is
questions.trick: $W=q(V_A-V_B)$; dropping potential (200$\to$50) gives positive work by the field.

questions.q: The work done in moving a charge along an equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: All points on an equipotential surface are at the same potential, so $W=q(V_A-V_B)=0$.
questions.trick: Equipotential surface → same $V$ everywhere → work done is always zero.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor has plate area 0.02 m$^2$ and separation 2 mm. Its capacitance in air is (take $\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}$ F/m)
questions.trick: $C=\varepsilon_0A/d$ — plug straight in, answer lands in pF range for cm-scale plates.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance 10 $\mu$F is charged to 100 V and then a dielectric slab of dielectric constant 5 is inserted between the plates while it remains connected to the battery. The new charge on the capacitor is
questions.explanation: Connected to battery, $V$ stays 100 V; $C' = KC = 50\,\mu$F; $Q' = C'V = 50\times100 = 5000\,\mu$C.
questions.trick: Battery stays connected → $V$ fixed, so $C,Q$ both scale by $K$.

questions.q: An isolated charged capacitor (battery disconnected) has a dielectric slab of dielectric constant 4 inserted between its plates. The energy stored
questions.explanation: With charge $Q$ fixed, $C$ becomes $4C$, so $U = Q^2/2C$ decreases to $U/4$.
questions.trick: Isolated capacitor → $Q$ fixed, $C\to KC$, so $U=Q^2/2C$ falls by factor $K$.

questions.q: Three capacitors of 2 $\mu$F, 3 $\mu$F and 6 $\mu$F are connected in series. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac1C = \dfrac12+\dfrac13+\dfrac16 = \dfrac{3+2+1}{6}=1 \Rightarrow C = 1\,\mu$F.
questions.trick: Series: reciprocal sum, and it's always LESS than the smallest capacitor.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 4 $\mu$F and 6 $\mu$F are connected in parallel across a 10 V battery. The total energy stored is
questions.explanation: $C_{eq} = 10\,\mu$F; $U = \dfrac12CV^2 = \dfrac12\times10\times10^{-6}\times100 = 500\,\mu$J.
questions.trick: Parallel: capacitances add first, then use $U=\frac12C_{eq}V^2$.

questions.q: The electric field inside a charged conductor in electrostatic equilibrium is
questions.explanation: In electrostatic equilibrium, free charges rearrange until the net field inside the conductor's material is zero.
questions.trick: Conductor in equilibrium: interior field is always exactly zero.

questions.q: A hollow metal sphere of radius 10 cm is charged such that the potential on its surface is 200 V. The potential at its centre is
questions.explanation: A conductor is an equipotential body; since the field inside is zero, the potential inside equals the surface potential, 200 V.
questions.trick: Conductor is equipotential: centre potential = surface potential, always.

questions.q: The SI unit of capacitance, the farad, is dimensionally equivalent to
questions.explanation: $C = Q/V$, so unit is coulomb per volt (C/V), defined as the farad.
questions.trick: Farad $=C/V$ by definition of $C=Q/V$ — no other combination.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor with air as dielectric has capacitance $C$. If the separation between plates is halved and a dielectric of constant $K=4$ completely fills the gap, the new capacitance is
questions.explanation: $C \propto K/d$. Halving $d$ doubles $C$; inserting $K=4$ multiplies by 4: net factor $= 2\times4 = 8$, so $C' = 8C$.
questions.trick: $C\propto K/d$: multiply the separate factors (halved $d$ $\times2$, $K=4$ $\times4$) $=8C$.

questions.q: Two identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C$, are first connected in series and then in parallel across the same battery of emf $V$. The ratio of energy stored in parallel to that in series is
questions.explanation: Series: $C_s=C/2$, $U_s=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{C}{2}V^2=\dfrac{CV^2}{4}$. Parallel: $C_p=2C$, $U_p=\dfrac12\cdot2C\cdot V^2=CV^2$. Ratio $U_p:U_s = 4:1$.
questions.trick: Same battery: $U_{parallel}/U_{series}=4$ for two identical capacitors — a memorisable ratio.

questions.q: The potential energy of a system of two point charges $+q$ and $-q$ separated by distance $r$ is
questions.explanation: $U = \dfrac{kq_1q_2}{r} = \dfrac{k(q)(-q)}{r} = -\dfrac{kq^2}{r}$ (negative, since opposite charges attract).
questions.trick: Opposite charges → $U$ is negative: $U=kq_1q_2/r$, sign follows charge product.

questions.q: In a Van de Graaff generator, charge sprayed onto the inside of a large hollow conducting sphere
options: remains uniformly distributed inside the volume
stays on the inner surface near the point of spraying
immediately moves to the outer surface of the sphere
questions.explanation: Charge given to a hollow conductor always moves to its outer surface, allowing the sphere's potential to keep rising as more charge is added.
questions.trick: Hollow conductor: sprayed charge always migrates entirely to the outer surface.

questions.q: The energy density of the electric field in vacuum is given by
questions.explanation: Energy stored per unit volume in an electric field is $u = \dfrac12\varepsilon_0E^2$.
questions.trick: Energy density formula: $\frac12\varepsilon_0E^2$ — same $\frac12$ pattern as $\frac12CV^2$.

questions.q: Equipotential surfaces due to an isolated point charge are
options: concentric spheres centred on the charge
planes perpendicular to the line joining the charge
questions.explanation: Since $V = kq/r$ depends only on distance $r$ from the point charge, surfaces of constant $V$ are concentric spheres.
questions.trick: Point charge equipotentials: concentric spheres, since $V$ depends only on $r$.

questions.q: A capacitor of 4 $\mu$F is charged to a potential difference of 50 V and then disconnected and connected in parallel to an uncharged 4 $\mu$F capacitor. The common potential is
questions.explanation: Charge is conserved: $Q = 4\times50 = 200\,\mu$C shared over total capacitance $8\,\mu$F; $V = 200/8 = 25$ V.
questions.trick: Charge conserves on parallel connection: total $Q$ over total $C$ gives common $V$.

questions.q: For two charges kept fixed, the electric potential energy of the system is negative. This implies
options: no work is needed to assemble the system
the charges are unlike charges and attract each other
the charges are at infinite separation
questions.explanation: $U = kq_1q_2/r$ is negative only when $q_1q_2<0$, i.e. unlike charges, which attract; external work would be needed to pull them apart to infinity.
questions.trick: Negative $U$ always means unlike (attracting) charges — sign of $q_1q_2$ tells all.

questions.q: The relationship between electric field $E$ and potential $V$ along a direction $r$ is given by
questions.explanation: The electric field is the negative gradient of potential: $E=-dV/dr$, pointing from high to low potential.
questions.trick: $E=-dV/dr$: the minus sign means field points toward decreasing potential.

questions.q: Two isolated conducting spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$, carrying some initial charges, are connected by a thin conducting wire until equilibrium. The ratio of the final charges on the smaller sphere to the larger sphere is
questions.explanation: At equilibrium the spheres reach the same potential: $kq_1/R = kq_2/(2R) \Rightarrow q_1/q_2 = R/2R = 1/2$; charge divides in proportion to radius.
questions.trick: Connected conductors reach common $V$: charge divides in proportion to radius $R$.

questions.q: Four equal charges of $+1\,\mu$C each are placed at the four corners of a square such that each corner is 10 cm from the centre. The electric potential at the centre is
questions.explanation: Potential is scalar: $V=4\times\dfrac{kq}{r}=4\times\dfrac{9\times10^9\times10^{-6}}{0.1}=4\times9\times10^4=3.6\times10^5$ V.
questions.trick: Potential is scalar: just multiply single-charge $V$ by the number of identical charges.

questions.q: The electric potential due to a short dipole of moment $p$ at a point on its axial line at distance $r$ ($r\gg$ dipole length) is
questions.explanation: The axial potential of a short dipole is $V=kp/r^2$, falling off faster than a monopole's $kq/r$ but slower than the equatorial value (which is zero).
questions.trick: Dipole axial potential is $kp/r^2$ — one power of $r$ less than the field.

questions.q: The electric potential due to a dipole at any point on its equatorial line (perpendicular bisector of the dipole axis) is
questions.explanation: Every point on the equatorial line is equidistant from $+q$ and $-q$, so their potentials cancel exactly, giving $V=0$.
questions.trick: Equatorial line is equidistant from $+q,-q$ → potential always exactly zero there.

questions.q: A capacitor is charged from a battery of emf $V$ through a resistor. If the total energy delivered by the battery is $W$, then the energy finally stored in the capacitor and the energy dissipated as heat in the resistor are respectively
questions.explanation: Regardless of the resistance value, exactly half the energy supplied by the battery ($QV$) ends up stored in the capacitor ($\tfrac12QV$), and the other half is dissipated as heat in the resistor.
questions.trick: Charging via a resistor: exactly half the battery's energy is always dissipated as heat.

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $C$ charged to potential $V$ is connected to an identical uncharged capacitor $C$. The loss of energy in the process is
questions.explanation: Common potential $=V/2$; final energy $=\dfrac12(2C)(V/2)^2=\dfrac14CV^2$; initial energy was $\dfrac12CV^2$, so the loss $=\dfrac12CV^2-\dfrac14CV^2=\dfrac14CV^2$ (dissipated during charge redistribution).
questions.trick: Sharing charge between capacitors always loses energy: use $\Delta U=\frac{C_1C_2}{2(C_1+C_2)}(V_1-V_2)^2$.

questions.q: For a parallel plate capacitor, if the plate area is doubled and the plate separation is also doubled, the capacitance
questions.explanation: $C\propto A/d$; doubling both $A$ and $d$ leaves the ratio, and hence $C$, unchanged.
questions.trick: $C\propto A/d$: doubling both leaves the ratio, hence $C$, unchanged.

questions.q: $n$ identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C$, connected in series give an equivalent capacitance of
questions.explanation: In series, $1/C_{eq}=n/C \Rightarrow C_{eq}=C/n$.
questions.trick: $n$ identical in series: $C_{eq}=C/n$ — divide by count.

questions.q: $n$ identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C$, connected in parallel give an equivalent capacitance of
questions.explanation: In parallel, capacitances simply add: $C_{eq}=nC$.
questions.trick: $n$ identical in parallel: $C_{eq}=nC$ — multiply by count.

questions.q: Two capacitors of 2 $\mu$F and 2 $\mu$F are connected in series, and this combination is connected in parallel with a third capacitor of 3 $\mu$F. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: Series combination of the two 2 $\mu$F capacitors gives $1\,\mu$F; this in parallel with 3 $\mu$F gives $1+3=4\,\mu$F.
questions.trick: Reduce series pairs first to a single value, then add parallel branches.

questions.q: The work done in charging a capacitor of capacitance $C$ from charge 0 to $Q$ is
questions.explanation: The work done in charging equals the energy stored, $U=\dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$ (not $QV$, since the charging voltage rises gradually from 0 to $V$).
questions.trick: Charging work $=Q^2/2C$, never $QV$ — the extra factor of 2 is the trap.

questions.q: In a region, the electric potential varies as $V = 200 - 50x$ (SI units), where $x$ is in metres. The electric field in that region is
questions.explanation: $E=-\dfrac{dV}{dx}=-(-50)=50$ N/C, directed along the +x direction (potential decreases as $x$ increases, so field points along increasing $x$).
questions.trick: $E=-dV/dx$ — read off the slope's negative directly from the linear $V(x)$ expression.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged and then disconnected from the battery. If the plates are now pulled further apart, the energy stored in the capacitor
questions.explanation: With charge $Q$ fixed, separating the plates decreases $C$ (since $C\propto1/d$), so $U=Q^2/2C$ increases; the extra energy comes from the work done in pulling the plates apart against their mutual attraction.
questions.trick: Isolated (Q fixed), plates pulled apart: $C$ falls so $U=Q^2/2C$ rises.

questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 5 pF (with air) is completely filled with a dielectric of dielectric constant 6. Its new capacitance is
questions.explanation: $C' = KC = 6\times5 = 30$ pF.
questions.trick: $C'=KC$ — dielectric constant is a direct multiplier on capacitance.

questions.q: The electric potential due to a point charge $-q$ at a distance $r$ from it is
questions.explanation: $V=kq'/r$ with $q'=-q$ gives $V=-kq/r$, negative for a negative source charge.
questions.trick: Negative source charge gives negative potential: $V=-kq/r$, sign follows the charge.

questions.q: The work done in moving a charge along a closed path in an electrostatic field is always
questions.explanation: The electrostatic field is conservative, so the net work done around any closed path is always zero.
questions.trick: Conservative field → net work round any closed loop is always zero.

questions.q: The dielectric constant $K$ of a medium is defined as the ratio of
options: electric field in vacuum to permittivity of the medium
capacitance with dielectric to capacitance without dielectric (vacuum), for the same capacitor
capacitance without dielectric to capacitance with dielectric, for the same capacitor
charge to voltage ratio in vacuum
questions.explanation: Dielectric constant $K=C_{medium}/C_{vacuum}$ for the same capacitor geometry; it is always $\ge1$.
questions.trick: $K=C_{medium}/C_{vacuum}$, always $\ge1$ — dielectric increases capacitance.

questions.q: Three identical capacitors, each of capacitance $C$, are connected such that two of them are in parallel, and this combination is connected in series with the third. The equivalent capacitance is
questions.explanation: Two in parallel give $2C$; in series with the third $C$: $C_{eq}=\dfrac{2C\times C}{2C+C}=\dfrac{2C}{3}$.
questions.trick: Combine parallel branch first ($2C$), then series formula with the third $C$.

questions.q: For a system of three point charges $q_1, q_2, q_3$ at mutual separations $r_{12}, r_{13}, r_{23}$, the total electrostatic potential energy of the system is
questions.explanation: The total potential energy is the sum of the pairwise potential energies over all pairs of charges.
questions.trick: Total PE of a charge system = sum over ALL distinct pairs, not just one.
